routes.label: Use the smaller cube of centers

question: Nine congruent spheres are packed inside a unit cube in such a way that one of them has its center at the center of the cube and each of the others is tangent to the center sphere and to three faces of the cube. What is the radius of each sphere?
solution:
Tangency to a face puts a sphere's center exactly one radius from that face. Let the common radius be \(r>0\). A sphere inside the unit cube has \(r\le\frac12\). Equality would force every center to be the cube's center, so nine spheres could not be packed that way. Thus \(r<\frac12\).

The three faces touching an outer sphere cannot include opposite faces, since tangency to opposite faces would require \(2r=1\). They therefore meet at a vertex. The sphere's center is \(r\) inward from each of these three faces.

There is one possible center position for each of the eight vertices. Distinct packed spheres cannot occupy the same position, so the eight outer centers form a smaller cube with side length
\[
s=1-2r.
\]
This smaller cube has the same center \(O\) as the original cube. Applying the Pythagorean theorem first to a face and then to a body diagonal shows that its body diagonal has length \(\sqrt3\,s\).

Each outer sphere is externally tangent to the central sphere, so its center is \(2r\) from \(O\). Since \(O\) bisects a body diagonal of the smaller cube, that diagonal also has length \(4r\). Consequently
\[
\sqrt3(1-2r)=4r.
\]
Solving and rationalizing gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
r&=\frac{\sqrt3}{2(2+\sqrt3)}\\
&=\frac{\sqrt3(2-\sqrt3)}{2}
=\frac{2\sqrt3-3}{2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This value satisfies \(0<r<\frac12\). The nearest outer centers are \(s\) apart, and
\[
s=\frac{4r}{\sqrt3}>2r,
\]
so the outer spheres do not overlap. All spheres fit inside the cube, and every outer sphere has the required tangencies. The radius is therefore \(\boxed{\frac{2\sqrt3-3}{2}}\), choice B.
